tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

entries.name: CronCreate
entries.description:
Schedule a prompt to be enqueued at a future time. Use for both recurring schedules and one-shot reminders.

Uses standard 5-field cron in the user's local timezone: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. "0 9 * * *" means 9am local — no timezone conversion needed.

## One-shot tasks (recurring: false)

For "remind me at X" or "at <time>, do Y" requests — fire once then auto-delete.
Pin minute/hour/day-of-month/month to specific values:
  "remind me at 2:30pm today to check the deploy" → cron: "30 14 <today_dom> <today_month> *", recurring: false
  "tomorrow morning, run the smoke test" → cron: "57 8 <tomorrow_dom> <tomorrow_month> *", recurring: false

## Recurring jobs (recurring: true, the default)

For "every N minutes" / "every hour" / "weekdays at 9am" requests:
  "*/5 * * * *" (every 5 min), "0 * * * *" (hourly), "0 9 * * 1-5" (weekdays at 9am local)

## Avoid the :00 and :30 minute marks when the task allows it

Every user who asks for "9am" gets `0 9`, and every user who asks for "hourly" gets `0 *` — which means requests from across the planet land on the API at the same instant. When the user's request is approximate, pick a minute that is NOT 0 or 30:
  "every morning around 9" → "57 8 * * *" or "3 9 * * *" (not "0 9 * * *")
  "hourly" → "7 * * * *" (not "0 * * * *")
  "in an hour or so, remind me to..." → pick whatever minute you land on, don't round

Only use minute 0 or 30 when the user names that exact time and clearly means it ("at 9:00 sharp", "at half past", coordinating with a meeting). When in doubt, nudge a few minutes early or late — the user will not notice, and the fleet will.

## Session-only

Jobs live only in this Claude session — nothing is written to disk, and the job is gone when Claude exits.

## Not for live watching

CronCreate re-runs a prompt at fixed wall-clock intervals. To watch a log file, process, or command output and be notified the moment something changes, use the Monitor tool instead — Monitor streams events as they happen; cron polls on a schedule.

## Runtime behavior

Jobs only fire while the REPL is idle (not mid-query). The scheduler adds a small deterministic jitter on top of whatever you pick: recurring tasks fire up to 10% of their period late (max 15 min); one-shot tasks landing on :00 or :30 fire up to 90 s early. Picking an off-minute is still the bigger lever.

Recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days — they fire one final time, then are deleted. This bounds session lifetime. Tell the user about the 7-day limit when scheduling recurring jobs.

Returns a job ID you can pass to CronDelete.

recurring.description: true (default) = fire on every cron match until deleted or auto-expired after 7 days. false = fire once at the next match, then auto-delete. Use false for "remind me at X" one-shot requests with pinned minute/hour/dom/month.

---
name: open-workflow-issues
description: Open workflow issues from workflow-guardrails-001 the user wants fixed before slice 3; list lives in ~/dev/md-manager-reviews/workflow-guardrails-001-issues.md
metadata:
  type: project
---

The user asked (2026-09-23) to record and fix every issue seen during the slice 2 run; they hit the Claude Code auto-update problem twice and want it fixed for good.

Checklist file: ~/dev/md-manager-reviews/workflow-guardrails-001-issues.md (P1: auto-update reinstall loop blocks controller + drops panes; P1: transient errors trigger worker stop; P2: pane reconnect, git worktree race, silent launch pane, runner log lost exception line; decisions on challenge edits/outside-graph/Herdr Enter).

**Why:** runs were blocked four times by reinstalls; the user considers the workflow not smooth until these are fixed.
**How to apply:** after workflow-guardrails-001 integrates, fix these (start from the uncommitted retry patch in ~/dev/md-manager-ctl2) before writing slice 3. See [[workflow-live-run-lessons]], [[portable-workflow-plan]].
---
name: workflow-live-run-lessons
description: Operational lessons from the first live automatic LangGraph workflow run (2026-09-21) that are not visible in the code
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 51a90443-d885-436e-98ca-f9604a2e21b3
  modified: 2026-09-21T15:52:42.538Z
---

First live automatic run of `python -m workflow launch project-workflows --live --automatic` completed on 2026-09-21: verified feature branch `feature/project-workflows/project-workflows-001` at b5385b3, reviewer approved with 6 P2 findings, no push. Run dir: `~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/project-workflows/project-workflows-001`.

**Why:** Several things only surfaced live and shape how future runs are operated.

**How to apply:**
- One-time setup: `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` must be accepted interactively once, or `claude --bg` with bypass exits 1.
- The source checkout is pinned to the feature branch at the base commit and must stay clean until integration. To run a *fixed* controller mid-run, use a separate worktree of `main` (e.g. `~/dev/md-manager-ctl`, symlink `node_modules`) and run `~/dev/md-manager/.venv/bin/python -m workflow ...` from there. Remove it after merging.
- To rerun failed lanes on the same snapshots: move `verification/` aside, delete `attempts.json`, then `git worktree prune` in the source repo (moved lane worktrees stay registered and block `worktree add`), delete any empty lane dirs, then `workflow retry <run>` followed by `workflow automatic <run> --live`.
- `workflow status` is refused while a supervisor step holds `controller.lock`; read `events.jsonl` / `report.html` instead.
- Worker transcripts live under `~/.claude/projects/<encoded worktree path>/<session uuid>.jsonl`; resume with `cd <worktree> && claude --resume <uuid>`. The `--name` label is not a resume key.
- Fixes committed to `main` from this run: launch-settle for late pid, Herdr pane shell settle, short lane TMPDIR (Unix socket 107-byte limit broke every tsx check), identical-failure retry stop, stale-task-error classifier. See [[md-manager-prd-tdd-workflow]].

- 2026-09-23: a Claude Code auto-update swaps the `claude` symlink; a controller call at that instant fails with `[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'claude'` and blocks the run while workers keep running. Resume with `python -m workflow automatic <run> --live` once `which claude` resolves. The worker panes' `attach-one` can also fail ("background service is unavailable … claude.exe (deleted)"); sessions survive in the restarted daemon, so rerun `python -m workflow.interactive attach-one <run> --node <lane>` in each pane (pane ids in terminals.json).
- Cause confirmed 2026-09-23: newly launched worker sessions run Claude Code's auto-updater (`npm install --global @anthropic-ai/claude-code@<same version>`), which recurs per session (19:33 and 19:42 in workflow-guardrails-001). Workaround: resume/launch the controller with `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`. Proposed permanent fix (after the run, never while the checkout is pinned): controller sets DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 for sessions it launches and retries a transient missing `claude` instead of blocking.
- Worker panes drop at every daemon restart; run attach-one in a `while true; do …attach-one…; sleep 3; done` loop in each pane so they reconnect themselves. The controller-side retry (run_claude, 60s grace) was validated live when a 19:57 reinstall caused no block.
---
name: worker-test-policy
description: User's decision on test runs in workflow tasks — workers run targeted tests only; the trusted verifier runs the full policy checks
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

The definition revision is a backend-generated SHA-256 of canonical definition JSON excluding `definition_revision` (sorted object keys, compact separators, UTF-8 literal Unicode; retain array order). def verify_revision(run: Path, plan: dict, policy: dict, node: str, commit: str, changed: list[str],
                    session_id: str, phase: str = "worker", attempt: int = 1) -> dict:
    """One fresh verification worktree per node/phase/attempt, artifacts retained."""
    worker = next(worker for worker in policy["workers"] if worker["node_id"] == node)
    directory = run / "verification" / phase / node / str(attempt)
    packet_path = directory / "packet.json"
    if packet_path.exists():
        packet = json.loads(packet_path.read_text())
        if packet["expected"]["output_commit"] != commit or packet["evidence"]["policy_sha256"] != policy_digest(policy):
            raise ValueError("Existing verification belongs to a different revision/policy")
        return recheck_packet(packet, policy, run)
    if directory.exists():
        raise RuntimeError("Interrupted check attempt exists; use an explicitly incremented attempt")
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, mode=0o700)
    worktree = directory / "worktree"
    subprocess.run(["git", "-C", plan["repository"], "worktree", "add", "--detach", str(worktree), commit], check=True, capture_output=True)
    if git(worktree, "rev-parse", "HEAD") != commit or git(worktree, "status", "--porcelain"):
        raise RuntimeError("Verification worktree did not start clean at expected revision")
    artifacts_dir = directory / "artifacts"
    artifacts_dir.mkdir()
    capture = Capture(artifacts_dir)
    # Captured before any check runs, so a check that rewrites a file cannot change what is recorded; the
    # post-check cleanliness rule below invalidates the evidence if one does. The candidate phase captures nothing.
    files_not_captured = capture_changed_files(worktree, changed, capture) if phase == "worker" else None
    env = {key: value for key, value in os.environ.items() if not key.startswith("HERDR_")}
    for key in list(env):
        if key.startswith("PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT"):
            del env[key]  # The runner owns JSON capture, not inherited reporter paths.
    # Share installed browser executables read-only, not profiles or test caches.
    if sys.platform == "linux":
        env.setdefault("PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH", str(Path(env.get("XDG_CACHE_HOME", str(Path.home() / ".cache"))) / "ms-playwright"))
    env.update(PATH=str(Path(sys.executable).parent) + os.pathsep + env.get("PATH", ""),
               PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1", NO_COLOR="1", FORCE_COLOR="0", CI="1",
               WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=phase)
    for name in ("XDG_CACHE_HOME", "npm_config_cache"):
        path = directory / name.lower()
        path.mkdir()
        env[name] = str(path)
    # Unix domain sockets (tsx IPC, Chromium) are limited to ~107 bytes of path, so the
    # lane's TMPDIR cannot live under the run directory. It is private to this lane,
    # holds no evidence, and is removed once the checks finish.
    tmpdir = lane_tmpdir()
    env["TMPDIR"] = str(tmpdir)
    executions, receipts, errors, effective_commands = [], [], [], []
    try:
        run_lane_commands(policy, worker, worktree, directory, env, capture, executions, receipts, errors, effective_commands)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmpdir, ignore_errors=True)
    # Source edits by checks invalidate the evidence. Ignored caches are allowed.
    if git(worktree, "rev-parse", "HEAD") != commit or git(worktree, "status", "--porcelain"):
        errors.append("Verification modified the tested source revision")
    expected = {"run_id": plan["run_id"], "node_id": node, "attempt": attempt, "base_commit": plan["base_commit"],
                "output_commit": commit, "verification_cwd": str(worktree)}
    result = {"contract_version": "1.0.0", **{key: value for key, value in expected.items() if key != "verification_cwd"},
              "session_id": session_id, "status": "succeeded", "changed_files": changed,
              "checks": executions, "open_assumptions": [], "artifacts": capture.artifacts,
              "summary": f"Trusted {phase} check capture; not integration approval", "error": None,
              **({"files_not_captured": files_not_captured} if files_not_captured is not None else {})}
    evidence = {"version": "1.0.0", "policy_sha256": policy_digest(policy),
                **{key: expected[key] for key in ("run_id", "node_id", "attempt", "output_commit")}, "checks": receipts}
    packet = {"phase": phase, "expected": expected, "result": result, "evidence": evidence,
              "artifact_root": str(artifacts_dir), "artifact_paths": {key: str(path) for key, path in capture.paths.items()},
              "capture_errors": errors, "effective_commands": effective_commands, "tmpdir": str(tmpdir)}
    packet = recheck_packet(packet, policy, run)
    save_json(packet_path, packet)
    return packet


SOCKET_PATH_LIMIT = 107  # sun_path on Linux, excluding the terminating NUL.
SOCKET_NAME_ALLOWANCE = len("/tsx-4294967295/4294967295.pipe")


def lane_tmpdir() -> Path:
    """A short private temp directory whose sockets fit within sun_path."""
    tmpdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="mdwf-"))
    if len(str(tmpdir)) + SOCKET_NAME_ALLOWANCE > SOCKET_PATH_LIMIT:
        shutil.rmtree(tmpdir, ignore_errors=True)
        raise RuntimeError(f"System temp directory is too deep for Unix sockets: {tmpdir.parent}")
    return tmpdir

                      executions: list, receipts: list, errors: list, effective_commands: list) -> None:
    for index, setup in enumerate(policy.get("setup", [])):
        log = directory / f"setup-{index}.log"
        code, _, _ = execute(setup["argv"], worktree, log, setup["timeout_seconds"], env)
        capture.add(log, "log")
        if code != 0:
            errors.append(f"Setup {index} failed with exit {code}")
            break
    if not errors:
        for index, check in enumerate(worker["checks"]):
            argv = list(check["argv"])
            log = directory / f"check-{index}.log"
            browser_output = directory / f"browser-{index}"
            browser_report = directory / f"browser-report-{index}.json"
            check_env = dict(env)
            if check["kind"] == "browser":
                # Runtime-owned reporter/output flags override project defaults.
                argv.extend(["--reporter=json", f"--output={browser_output}", "--workers=1", "--retries=0"])
                check_env["PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_FILE"] = str(browser_report)
            effective_commands.append(argv)
            code, start, finish = execute(argv, worktree, log, check["timeout_seconds"], check_env)
            log_id = capture.add(log, "log")
            executions.append({"command": shlex.join(check["argv"]), "cwd": str(worktree),
                               "started_at": start, "finished_at": finish, "exit_code": code, "log_artifact_id": log_id})
            tests, scenarios = None, []
            try:
                if check["kind"] == "browser":
                    if not browser_report.exists():
                        # Playwright writes its report only once the suite starts; a config or fixture
                        # error leaves none. Say so without quoting a path that differs per attempt.
                        raise ValueError(f"no Playwright report written (exit {code}); the suite did not start")
                    # Keep structured results separate from npm/Node warnings in logs.
                    tests, scenarios = browser_evidence(browser_report, browser_output, check, capture)
                    capture.add(browser_report, "test_report")
                elif check["kind"] in {"unit", "contract", "integration"}:
                    tests = text_test_counts(log.read_text(errors="replace"))
                if code != 0:
                    errors.append(f"{check['id']}: exit {code}")
            except (ValueError, OSError, KeyError, TypeError) as error:
                errors.append(f"{check['id']}: {error}")
            receipts.append({"id": check["id"], "worker_check_index": index, "tests": tests, "scenarios": scenarios})

def recheck_packet(packet: dict, policy: dict, run: Path) -> dict:
    root = Path(packet["artifact_root"]).resolve()
    if not root.is_relative_to(run.resolve()):
        raise ValueError("Artifact root outside run")
    gate = evaluate_worker(policy, packet["result"], packet["evidence"], expected=packet["expected"],
                           artifact_root=root, artifact_paths={key: Path(value) for key, value in packet["artifact_paths"].items()},
                           enforce_ownership=packet["phase"] == "worker", phase=packet["phase"])
    # Capture errors are prefixed with their check id; a deferred check's errors are evidence, not a gate.
    deferred_prefixes = tuple(f"{check_id}{separator}" for check_id in gate["deferred_checks"] for separator in (":", "/"))
    gate["reasons"].extend(error for error in packet["capture_errors"] if not error.startswith(deferred_prefixes))
    if gate["reasons"]:
        gate["status"] = "blocked"
    packet["gate"] = gate
    return packet

    `expected` is backend-owned: run_id, node_id, attempt, base_commit,
    output_commit and verification_cwd. Caller must freeze edits and independently
    derive the full Git diff/commit before invoking; this function cannot prove
    that an agent has reported all changed files.

    In the `worker` phase, checks of a DEFERRED_WORKER_KINDS kind are verified for
    integrity (approved argv, worktree, timeout) and recorded, but their outcome does
    not gate; the returned `deferred_checks` names them. Every other phase gates on all.
    """
    reasons = []
    deferred = []
    try:
        validate_policy(policy)

def recheck_packet(packet: dict, policy: dict, run: Path) -> dict:
    root = Path(packet["artifact_root"]).resolve()
    if not root.is_relative_to(run.resolve()):
        raise ValueError("Artifact root outside run")
    gate = evaluate_worker(policy, packet["result"], packet["evidence"], expected=packet["expected"],
                           artifact_root=root, artifact_paths={key: Path(value) for key, value in packet["artifact_paths"].items()},
                           enforce_ownership=packet["phase"] == "worker", phase=packet["phase"])
    # Capture errors are prefixed with their check id; a deferred check's errors are evidence, not a gate.
    deferred_prefixes = tuple(f"{check_id}{separator}" for check_id in gate["deferred_checks"] for separator in (":", "/"))
    gate["reasons"].extend(error for error in packet["capture_errors"] if not error.startswith(deferred_prefixes))
    if gate["reasons"]:
        gate["status"] = "blocked"
    packet["gate"] = gate
    return packet

    `expected` is backend-owned: run_id, node_id, attempt, base_commit,
    output_commit and verification_cwd. Caller must freeze edits and independently
    derive the full Git diff/commit before invoking; this function cannot prove
    that an agent has reported all changed files.

    In the `worker` phase, checks of a DEFERRED_WORKER_KINDS kind are verified for
    integrity (approved argv, worktree, timeout) and recorded, but their outcome does
    not gate; the returned `deferred_checks` names them. Every other phase gates on all.

The end-to-end test uses real temporary Git worktrees, Python unit tests, headless Chromium, screenshot files, review/approval interrupts and a fast-forward of a **temporary test repository**. It makes no Claude model calls. A second test injects a check failure, reopens checkpoints and verifies that only the failed verification attempt reruns. The automatic tests run once with the native reviewer protocol and once with the print-mode fallback, each with the single built-in reviewer and with two declared reviewers, including a controller interrupted while waiting for the reviewers and every rejected completion file; `ParallelReviewerScenarios` covers PRD_PARALLEL_REVIEWERS section 6 (two approve, one blocks, a P1 anywhere, one times out, a file naming the other reviewer, a shared session UUID, an interrupted second launch) and `test_lanes` the manual import per reviewer.
231:- **Interruption.** Ctrl-C, a closed terminal or a dropped SSH session while the controller waits leaves every reviewer running with `automatic-review.json` at `running`; `python -m workflow automatic "$RUN" --live` resumes waiting for the same sessions' files. The same holds inside a launch window once that reviewer's `claude --bg` was issued (its `.interactive.json` exists): the receipt is `running`, without `session_id` when the interrupt hit the settle poll, and resume rebinds that one session through reconciliation, never a relaunch. An interrupt before a reviewer's launch was issued leaves the run at `needs_reconciliation`: resume rebinds the reviewers that were launched and launches nothing, so the run cannot continue; stop the running reviewers by their exact ids and start a new run.
237:cd "$RUN/review-worktree" && claude --resume <reviewer-uuid>
240:The UUID is `session_id` in `$RUN/<node>.interactive.json` (or that reviewer's entry in `review.json`). Claude keeps transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/<encoded worktree path>/<uuid>.jsonl`, keyed by the worktree the session ran in, which is why the resume must start from `review-worktree`, the checkout every reviewer of the run shared.
267:- **Failure after stopping/snapshotting or integrating:** `retry "$RUN"` resumes only failed graph steps; it never launches a new Claude worker. Stop-intent recovery checks whether the prior stop already completed before issuing another native stop.

groups.task:
Issue list sections: "P1: Claude Code auto-update breaks running workflows" and "P1: a transient error during the worker wait tries to stop the workers".

Already done on this branch (commit 8c6d1e1, keep it): `run_claude` in workflow/sessions.py retries ENOENT/ENOEXEC/ETXTBSY (and, with retry_output, an empty `claude agents --json` listing) for up to 60s, only when the command did not run; interactive.inventory() and the pipeline stop call use it.

Do:
1. Route every other Claude CLI invocation the controller makes through run_claude: `claude --bg` launches (workers, native reviewers), `claude --print`/`-p` jobs (print reviewers, the design challenge job in workflow/guardrails.py run_challenge), `claude attach` where the controller starts it, and any other `claude` subprocess (grep for the executable/`sessions.executable`/"claude" in subprocess calls under workflow/). For launches and print jobs, retry ONLY an OSError raised before the process started (the exec failed); never retry after the command ran and never pass retry_output, so a session or job can never start twice. Add tests per call site that a missing binary during the grace is retried and a launch that ran is not.
2. Every Claude process the controller starts gets DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 in its environment (workers, native and print reviewers, the challenge job, attach, agents/stop listings): implement it once centrally (for example in run_claude, merging into kwargs['env'] or os.environ) so a new call site cannot miss it, and test that each launch path passes it. Do not drop other env the call sites set.
3. Preflight warning: before `launch`/`start`/`resume` launch sessions (find the existing preflight checks, likely workflow/launch.py or pipeline start), scan running processes for Claude Code executables that were deleted by an update (Linux: /proc/<pid>/exe readlink ending in ' (deleted)' whose target path looks like a Claude Code binary, e.g. contains 'claude'); print one warning naming each pid, its cwd and command line, saying these long-lived sessions keep reinstalling Claude Code and should be restarted before the run. Warning only, never a refusal; silently skip on non-Linux or unreadable /proc entries. Make the /proc root injectable and test it with a fake tree.
4. Transient errors in the worker wait: today, when the automatic controller hits any exception while waiting for workers (see automatic.py wait_handoffs and the freeze path), it tries to stop the worker sessions (events showed `freeze blocked: Could not confirm worker stop`); had the stop succeeded, a missing `claude` binary would have killed two hours of worker time. Introduce one exception type for transient infrastructure failure (e.g. TransientInfraError raised when run_claude's grace is exhausted for ENOENT/ENOEXEC/ETXTBSY, when `claude agents --json` stays empty/unparseable/times out, or the background service is unavailable) and classify by type, not message text. On a transient error during the worker wait (and anywhere else in the automatic step where a transient failure would lead to stopping sessions), do not stop any session: record a timeline event (e.g. status `interrupted` with the cause), leave everything resumable and exit with code 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL) with a message telling the operator to rerun `python -m workflow automatic <run> --live` once `claude` works. Real verdicts (deadline exhausted, a lane `blocked`, an invalid completion, identity mismatches) keep today's behaviour. Check how the supervisor (`automatic --live`) runs `automatic-step` subprocesses and treats their exit codes, so 75 propagates as resumable rather than blocked, and whether 75 is already used. Tests: transient error in the wait -> no stop call, exit 75, run resumes cleanly afterwards; deadline -> stop as before.
5. RUNBOOK: operator practice: update Claude Code between runs, not during them; restart long-lived Claude sessions after an update (the preflight warning names them); the controller sets DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 for sessions it starts; what exit 75 means and how to resume.

groups.task:
Issue list section: "P1: the verifier's browser rules are hidden from the lanes until the candidate" (the first two bullets; the relaunch bullet is designed elsewhere).

What happened: the ui lane's `[scenario:inert-markdown]` test passed but attached `screenshot:inert-markdown-file` and `screenshot:inert-markdown-decisions` instead of one `screenshot:inert-markdown`, so the trusted verifier's browser_evidence (workflow/checks.py) raised 'Expected one screenshot attachment for inert-markdown'. In the worker phase browser checks are deferred (workflow/verification.py DEFERRED_WORKER_KINDS; checks.recheck_packet drops deferred checks' capture errors), so the rule was first enforced on the frozen candidate and the run ended blocked. The exact rule: each required scenario id appears in exactly one test title as `[scenario:<id>]`; a passed scenario test (status expected, one result, no retries) has exactly one attachment named `screenshot:<id>` with contentType image/png, inside the verifier's output dir; other attachments with other names are fine.

Do:
1. Move the scenario rules of browser_evidence into one pure function shared by the verifier and a new worker-facing command, so the two cannot diverge. The verifier's behaviour, messages and existing tests stay unchanged.
2. Add `python -m workflow check-report <feature-dir or policy.json> <lane> <report.json> [--all]` (wire it in workflow/__main__.py like init/resume/answer): validates a Playwright JSON report against that lane's browser check scenarios, prints one line per required scenario (ok / not in this report / the problem, with the same wording as the verifier), and exits 1 on any problem. Scenarios missing from the report (a worker ran only some spec files) are listed as not in this report and fail only with --all. It checks that each screenshot file exists but not that it lives under the verifier's output dir. Tests with synthetic JSON reports: valid; two screenshots with other names (this run's case); a missing screenshot; a duplicated title; a failing test; a partial report with and without --all; a lane without browser checks (clear message).
3. In the worker phase, evidence-shape errors of scenario tests that PASSED (wrong/missing/duplicate `screenshot:<id>`, a duplicated scenario title) are the lane's own fault, not a cross-lane dependency: make them gate in the worker phase too, while the browser check's exit status, failing tests and a report that was never written stay deferred as today. Keep error text prefixed with the check id. Test both halves (a passed test with two wrongly named screenshots blocks the worker phase; a suite that did not start or a failing test stays deferred).
4. Tell the lanes the rules where they read them, with the exact commands: the browser-lane task template written by `workflow init` (workflow/scaffold.py), the README/RUNBOOK section on writing features and tasks, and the test-section convention of docs/PRD_PORTABLE_WORKFLOW.md (where section 6 or 4.x describes browser scenarios). The worker command: `WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=<worker|candidate> PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_FILE=<tmp>/report.json npx --no-install playwright test --config=<config> --reporter=json <spec files>` then `python -m workflow check-report features/<feature> <lane> <tmp>/report.json`. If the controller appends text to lane tasks (the 'Approved ownership and checks' block, see sessions.prepare / guardrails.pinned_task), add one sentence there for lanes with browser scenarios pointing at check-report. Do not edit features/ (finished runs' feature folders).

groups.area: a per-repository lock around every git worktree add/remove/prune in workflow/ (checks.py verify_revision, sessions/pipeline worktree creation and cleanup)
groups.task:
Issue list section: "P2: `git worktree add` race when lanes verify at the same time".

What happened: workflow.test_lanes.DeclaredReviewers.test_manual_import_requires_every_declared_reviewer_before_approval failed once in verification with `git worktree add ... returned non-zero exit status 128` and passed on rerun; concurrent worktree creation in one repository collides on git's locks, and live runs verify both lanes at the same moment (20:08:49 in the run).

Do:
1. Add one helper that runs `git worktree add|remove|prune|move` (and `git worktree repair` if used) for a repository under an exclusive per-repository lock held across processes and threads: an fcntl lock file in the repository's git common dir (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, so linked worktrees of one repo share it), named generically (e.g. workflow-worktree.lock) since the tool is used on other projects too. Also retry a bounded number of times (short backoff) when git fails with a lock-contention message caused by processes outside our control (e.g. "could not lock", ".lock': File exists", "is locked"), and on final failure raise with git's stderr included in the message (today CalledProcessError with capture_output hides it).
2. Replace every `git worktree` subprocess call under workflow/ (grep: checks.py verify_revision, sessions.prepare/lane worktrees, candidate and review-worktree creation, challenge worktree in guardrails.py, cleanup/prune paths, tests' helpers only if they race) with the helper. Keep the call sites' semantics (detach, paths, check=True).
3. Tests: many (e.g. 8-12) worktrees created concurrently from threads AND from separate processes against one temporary repository all succeed and are registered; the lock is actually exclusive (a second holder blocks until release); a simulated lock-contention failure is retried and a persistent one raises with stderr in the message. Keep the test fast (< ~10 s).
4. Stay out of run_claude/DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER (autoupdate branch) and the check-report work (browser-rules branch).

Issue list section: "P2: worker panes do not survive a service restart" (and the related notes in the auto-update P1 section, point 2).

What happened: each Claude Code reinstall restarted the background service, which dropped every pane running `python -m workflow.interactive attach-one <run> --node <lane>` with "Couldn't reconnect to <id> — background service is unavailable … claude.exe (deleted)". The sessions survived (the restarted service adopts them), but the operator saw dead panes and had to rerun attach-one by hand. A manual `while true; do attach-one; sleep 3; done` loop then spammed "Session unavailable; refusing implicit restart" endlessly after the controller stopped the sessions on purpose at the freeze.

Do:
1. Make attach-one reconnect by itself: after `claude attach <session>` returns, decide from the run's own records and the live session inventory what happened. (a) The operator detached on purpose (find out how `claude attach` signals a user detach vs a lost connection: exit status and/or the inventory; check `claude attach --help` and try `claude attach <nonexistent-id>` to see its exit status without starting any session; never start a real session) -> exit quietly. (b) The session is still alive and the controller has not stopped it -> print one line (e.g. 'Lost the connection to <lane> (<id>); the background service may be restarting. Reattaching in Ns…') and reattach with a bounded backoff (a few seconds, capped), for as long as the session stays alive and not stopped; give up with a clear message after a generous limit of consecutive failures. (c) The controller stopped the session on purpose (the freeze/stop records the pipeline keeps: <node>.interactive.json status, stop intent/receipts, events.jsonl) -> print once 'Worker <lane> was stopped by the controller at <time> (<reason>); nothing to attach.' and exit 0. (d) The session is gone without a recorded stop -> print the existing refusal once and exit non-zero; never restart a session implicitly.
2. Ctrl-C in the pane ends attach-one cleanly (no traceback, no reattach).

4. groups.task:
Issue list section "To decide", first two bullets. The operator has decided both; implement the decisions.

A) Edits made to answer a design challenge must not leave the pinned source checkout dirty. Today (see workflow/guardrails.py resume_challenge, repin, pin_guardrails; RUNBOOK 'Rerun after an edit') the operator edits the lane task files, decisions.md or the PRD in the source checkout, runs `python -m workflow resume <run>`, which re-reads and re-pins them, but the edits stay uncommitted and integration later refuses the dirty checkout; the RUNBOOK tells them to stash by hand. Decision: `resume` commits them. Design: resume already refuses once any worker was launched, so no lane has any work yet. When the source checkout has changes, allow only the paths resume re-pins (the pinned task files, decisions.md, the PRD copy's source, anything else pin_guardrails reads); anything else dirty -> refuse and list the paths. Commit exactly those paths on the source checkout's feature branch (the pinned source_branch; verify HEAD is still the plan's base_commit on that branch first) with a message like 'Workflow <run>: feature files revised after design challenge attempt <n>' using the same git identity/commit conventions the pipeline already uses for its own commits. Then move the run to the new base: set the plan's base_commit to the new commit, move every lane worktree (and the challenge/any other run worktree created from the base) to it — each must still be clean and at the old base, refuse otherwise — and recompute everything derived from the base or the plan (observed_start_commit, plan/policy digests, receipts that bind to the plan digest; find them all: sessions.prepare, pipeline, export_state) exactly as a fresh prepare would, then re-pin and rerun the challenge as today. Crash safety: a resume interrupted between the commit and the re-pin must be rerunnable (detect the already-made commit and continue) and must never launch workers against a half-moved run. With --accept-challenge: if pinned files are dirty, refuse (the edits would not be part of the run: rerun without --accept-challenge to use them, or revert them); with a clean checkout it behaves as today. If you find moving the base unsafe somewhere you cannot fix, stop and report precisely why instead of shipping a partial version. Tests: an edited task file is committed, the checkout is clean, the lane worktrees and plan point at the new base, workers then launch on it and a later integration fast-forwards (use the existing end-to-end fakes); an unrelated dirty file is refused; --accept-challenge with dirty pinned files is refused; an interrupted resume continues. Update the RUNBOOK (remove the stash advice) and README.
B) The challenge runs inside start/resume, outside LangGraph, and appears in the exported graph as a `challenge` node; PRD 4.5 describes a graph node. Decision: keep the code, fix the documents. Update docs/PRD_PORTABLE_WORKFLOW.md 4.5 (and any README/RUNBOOK sentence that says it is a LangGraph node) to state where it runs, why (it must finish before any worker session exists and has its own pause/resume), and that the export shows it as the first node.
C) The Herdr key name used by `workflow answer` (`herdr pane send-keys <pane> Enter`) was verified live by the operator on 2026-09-23 against Claude Code 2.1.281's prompt: send-text followed by send-keys Enter submits the prompt. No code change; if the RUNBOOK's answer section has a caveat saying it is unverified, remove it.

content.text: Next, a small design panel for the one open decision: how to repair a single lane after the run blocks. It's read-only; the output is a design doc for me to decide from.

input.script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'lane-repair-design',
  description: 'Judge panel: three independent designs for repairing one lane of a blocked workflow run, scored and synthesized into a design doc',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Design', detail: 'three designers, different angles' },
    { title: 'Judge', detail: 'score and synthesize the recommended design' },
  ],
}

const REPO = '/home/agentops/dev/md-manager'
const CONTEXT = `Repository: ${REPO} (Python package workflow/, the LangGraph-based automatic controller; read workflow/README.md and workflow/RUNBOOK.md first, then workflow/pipeline.py, workflow/automatic.py, workflow/sessions.py, workflow/interactive.py, workflow/checks.py, workflow/verification.py, workflow/integration*.py or wherever the candidate is built). Read-only: do not edit anything in the repository or any run directory; do not run git commands that change state; no tests needed.

Problem (from /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-reviews/workflow-guardrails-001-issues.md, P1 'the verifier's browser rules are hidden from the lanes until the candidate', third bullet): in run workflow-guardrails-001 (run dir ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/workflow-guardrails/workflow-guardrails-001; read its plan.json, events.jsonl, verification/*/*/*/packet.json, attempts.json, checkpoint files as examples) both lanes finished and passed worker-phase verification, the combined candidate was integrated, and the candidate check of the ui lane failed twice identically on a one-line test defect ('Expected one screenshot attachment for inert-markdown'). The worker sessions had been stopped and their snapshots frozen; the identical-failure guard ended the run blocked. There is no supported way to send one lane back for a fix: \`retry\` reruns checks at the same revision and never launches a worker; \`reconcile\` never launches. About 2.5 to 3.5 hours from now (it's 21:03 UTC), so everything should be merged and verified by about 23:30–00:30 UTC. The slowest items could push that later.

| Track | Now | Estimate |
|---|---|---|
| Slice 2 review | 2 of 5 reviewers done; their findings are being checked | ~30–45 min |
| Lane-repair design | 3 designers working, then a judge | ~30 min |
| Issue fixes, workflow 1: autoupdate, browser-rules, worktree-lock | first two being built; autoupdate has its retry commit | ~1.5–2 h |
| Issue fixes, workflow 2: attach-reconnect, operator-visibility, challenge-resume | operator-visibility has one commit; attach-reconnect in progress | ~1.5–2 h |

Each fix goes through three steps: build, then an independent check, then one repair round if the check finds problems. Each workflow runs only two agents at a time on this 4-CPU machine, which is the main limit.

After the workflows finish, the remaining steps are:
- **Slice 2 review fixes:** ~20–30 min, depending on how many findings hold up.
- **Merging the six fix branches** onto the feature branch and resolving conflicts: ~20–30 min.
- **One full pass of every policy check** for both lanes and both phases (full test suites, build, all browser tests): ~30 min.
- **Merge to main.**

The biggest risks to the estimate:
- **challenge-resume** (moving the run to a new base after `resume`) is the trickiest change and may need a second round.
- **The final full check** could fail and need a rerun, which adds about 30 minutes.

lastPrompt: How much of this time is actually the agentts writing code vs the tests running

content.text:
Almost all of it is the agents thinking and writing code. Test time is small so far.

I measured the ten agents that have run so far (about 93 agent-minutes, 20:52 to 21:04 UTC):

| | Share of agent time |
|---|---|
| Agents reading code, reasoning and writing edits | ~89% (83 min) |
| Other tool calls (git, grep, file reads) | ~8% (8 min) |
| Running tests | ~3% (3 min) |

Some per-agent examples:
- **autoupdate:** 12 minutes in, it has spent 10.5 of them thinking and writing, with no tests run yet.
- **attach-reconnect:** 1.3 minutes of tests out of 11.5.
- **Reviewers and designers:** no tests at all; it's all reading and reasoning.

The test share will grow somewhat, but it stays the smaller part:
- **During the workflows:** implementers run their targeted tests near the end, and the checkers rerun them. That's probably 10–15% of workflow time.
- **After the workflows:** the final verification of both lanes in both phases is about 30 minutes of pure test time.

For the remaining ~3 hours, that works out to roughly 45 minutes of tests and about 2¼ hours of agent work. Targeted tests are doing their job: in the slice 1 run, tests were about 60% of the time.

The time goes to agents because:
- **The controller code is large.** Each agent reads a lot of `workflow/` before it can change it safely.
- **Every agent runs Opus at high effort,** including the checkers.
- **Only two agents run at a time per workflow,** so groups queue behind each other.

If you want it faster, the main lever is lighter models or lower effort for the checking and repair steps. That would roughly halve those steps, at some risk of missing subtle bugs. I'd keep the implementers and the slice 2 reviewers on Opus.

content.text:
More than two are already running. The limit of two applies inside each workflow, not overall. I started four workflows, so eight agents are working right now:

| Workflow | Running now | Queued |
|---|---|---|
| Slice 2 review | 2 reviewers or finding checkers | the rest of the 5 reviewers and their checks |
| Issue fixes 1 | autoupdate, browser-rules | worktree-lock |
| Issue fixes 2 | attach-reconnect, operator-visibility | challenge-resume |
| Lane-repair design | 2 designers | 1 designer, then the judge |

**Why a workflow runs only two at once.** The Workflow tool sets its per-workflow limit from the CPU count: CPUs minus 2, and this VPS has 4. That rule assumes agents do CPU-heavy work locally, like test suites, builds and Playwright. Here they mostly wait on the model: 89% of their time so far. The load average is 1.5 on 4 cores, with 4.3 GB of memory free, so the machine could take more agents right now.

**Why I didn't just launch one agent per item.** The real local limit shows up when tests pile up. If six implementers and the final verification all ran test suites and Playwright together on 4 cores, the checks could hit their timeouts and fail for no real reason. The `git worktree` race we saw in this run was a load problem too.

**What's still queued.** worktree-lock and challenge-resume will start when a slot frees, probably within 5–15 minutes. Starting them sooner would mean stopping agents that are 15 minutes into their work, so it costs more than it saves at this point.

**For next time.** I'll split independent work into more workflows from the start, about one per group. For the next feature run (slice 3), the same applies to worker lanes: they are Claude sessions, not limited by this rule, so running more of them in parallel is mostly about how the feature is split.

lastPrompt: So how many agents can safely run parallely with my current config?

content.text:
About 8 to 10 agents writing code, but only 2 heavy test runs at a time. Measured on this VPS: 4 cores, 7.9 GB RAM, about 4.3 GB free.

**The agents themselves cost almost nothing locally.** All 8 workflow agents run inside my one Claude process (about 500 MB in total), and they spend nearly all their time waiting on the model. With 8 running now, the load average is 1.5 of 4 and CPU pressure is about 8%, with no memory pressure.

**The limit is what the agents run:**

| What | Local cost | Safe at once |
|---|---|---|
| Agents reading, reasoning and editing | a few tens of MB each, almost no CPU | **8–10** |
| Targeted test runs (a few modules) | 1 core, under 100 MB, seconds to 2 min | 4–6 |
| Full workflow suite (`run_tests`) | all 4 cores for ~3.5 min | **1** |
| Playwright suite (Chromium plus servers) | 2 cores, 1–1.5 GB | **1–2** |
| Feature-run worker sessions (separate `claude --bg` processes) | 300–500 MB each | **3–4 lanes**, plus the verifier's Playwright run |

**Rule of thumb for this machine:** up to about 10 agents in parallel, as long as no more than 2 heavy test runs overlap. More than that makes checks time out or flake, the way the `git worktree` race did.

**The other ceiling is your plan's usage.** You're on Claude Max, and eight Opus agents at high effort use your 5-hour quota about eight times as fast as a single session. That's more likely to stop us than the CPU. I can't see your remaining usage; `/usage` in Claude Code should show it.

**How I'd use this:**
- **Workflows:** since each one runs only two agents at once, I'll split independent work into more workflows from the start (about one per group), for up to about 8–10 agents total, and keep full test runs and Playwright one at a time.
- **Feature runs (slice 3 on project-B):** up to 3–4 worker lanes in parallel is safe, which is a design choice when splitting the feature.

Right now we're at 8 agents with room to spare. The two queued groups will start as soon as a slot frees.

content.text:
Sleep well, I'll finish it overnight. Everything stays local: I'll never push. The plan, in order:

1. **Slice 2 review:** when the reviews finish, fix every finding that survives the independent checks on the feature branch.
2. **Issue fixes:** wait for all six groups to be built, checked and repaired. Then rebase each branch onto the feature branch and resolve conflicts.
3. **Lane repair:** if the design panel recommends a reasonably small first version, I'll build and check it too. If it's too big or risky, I'll leave it as a written decision for you instead.
4. **Final verification:** run every policy check for both lanes in both phases, using the verifier's own code, on the combined result. I'll run heavy tests one at a time so load doesn't cause false failures.
5. **Merge:** fast-forward main locally only if every check passes. If something fails and I can't fix it cleanly, main stays untouched and I'll write down exactly what failed.
6. **Handoff:** tick off everything in `~/dev/md-manager-reviews/workflow-guardrails-001-issues.md`. When you're back you'll get a short report: what landed, the commits, the check results, and anything left for you to decide.

# Lane repair after freeze: recommended design

Judged 2026-09-23 against `workflow/` at 7c5e37e and the run directory of workflow-guardrails-001 (read only). The LangGraph behaviour was re-probed on copies of that run's `pipeline.sqlite` with the pinned langgraph 1.2.11. The run directory was not touched.

## Recommendation

- **The command.** Add one operator command, `python -m workflow repair "$RUN" <lane>[,<lane>] --commit <sha> --reason "<text>"`. It turns an operator-made fix commit into a NEW lane snapshot, after the lane was frozen and blocked at `verify_<lane>` or at the combined candidate, and before any review bundle exists.
- **How the fix enters the graph.** `repair` forks the same LangGraph thread at the freeze-boundary checkpoint (`update_state(fork.config, {"snapshots": ...}, as_node="handoff")`). It launches nothing and runs no checks.
- **How the run continues.** `automatic --live` (or `retry` for a manual run) re-verifies through the unchanged graph:
  - the repaired lane gets a fresh worker-phase attempt;
  - unchanged lanes are rechecked;
  - a new candidate generation is checked for every lane, and only then does review happen.
- **Operator help.** A small `--workspace` helper creates a detached worktree at the right base (the failing candidate, or the lane snapshot) with a brief of the blocking reasons. That removes the foot-gun that broke 001's hand finish: committing on the pinned source branch.
- **The worker relaunch comes later.** The relaunch the issue list asks for (a new worker session seeded with the reasons and the task) is phase 2, as `repair --session --live`. It reuses the same apply path, and it lands only after fix/autoupdate, so that a transient CLI error cannot stop a repair session.

## Scores

Each criterion is scored 1–5, where 5 is best. For "size and risk", 5 means small and low risk.

| Design | Safety vs invariants | Crash recovery | Operator simplicity | Size and risk | Would have saved 001 | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| operator-amend (`amend --commit`) | 5 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 5 | **24** |
| risk-first (`repair` + new thread) | 5 | 4 | 3 | 3 | 5 | 20 |
| worker-relaunch (`relaunch` session) | 4 | 4 | 4 | 2 | 4 | 18 |

- **operator-amend:**
  - its core claims are correct and it is the smallest;
  - its journal and deterministic snapshot commit make every step idempotent;
  - the operator has to create their own worktree, and the design has no guard against committing on the pinned checkout (it can only refuse afterwards).
- **risk-first:**
  - it has the best operator ergonomics (a controller-made worktree at the failing revision);
  - its defensive assertions are good: the bundle's packet and snapshot commits must match, and the new candidate tree must equal the repaired tree;
  - its thread-per-generation premise is partly wrong (see the claims below);
  - it forces an "active thread" resolver into `graph_config`, `export_run` and `drive`;
  - its minimal version also needs an export 1.6.0 bump plus a server change;
  - its ref namespace `refs/workflow/<h>/repair-<n>/<lane>` collides with a legal lane id `repair-1`.
- **worker-relaunch:**
  - it has the most thorough analysis: 312a96d's defects, the combined-worktree need, and reviewer independence via `prior_session_ids`;
  - it is the only one that delivers the session the issue list asked for;
  - its minimal version already needs a new launch authority after freeze (receipts, a wait, a stop, a capture, a drive hook);
  - at about 450 production lines it is roughly twice the size of an operator commit path;
  - in session mode it spends a model session on what was a one-line fix;
  - its ref `<lane>-repair-<k>` can collide with a lane literally named `ui-repair-1`.

### Claims checked

1. **Verified: updating the head checkpoint is wrong.** On a copy of 001's database, `update_state(<thread config>, ..., as_node="handoff")` gave `next == (verify_controller, verify_ui, candidate)`. The candidate ran in the same superstep as the verifies, with the NEW snapshots and the OLD packets (`worker/ui/1`). In the real `Pipeline.candidate` it would then reuse `candidate.json` (1ab6b95) and could write a bundle for the unfixed candidate.
2. **Verified: forking at the freeze boundary is right.** Forking from `1f1b78a9-7767-6157-8002-fd9d42c806c9` (step 2, `next == verify fan-out`) with its own `checkpoint_id` gave:
   - `next == (verify_controller, verify_ui)`, `packets == {}`, no errors;
   - the candidate then ran once, after both verifies;
   - a second fork found the first fork (source `update`) as the newest fan-out checkpoint and worked the same way;
   - the fork head has metadata `source: update`, and its parent is `1f1b78a9…`.

   Pending writes are not carried into a fork when the config carries a `checkpoint_id`.
3. **Verified, but not a reason to prefer it: seeding an empty new thread also works.** The result was `next == verify fan-out`, and the old thread was unchanged. Risk-first's reason for rejecting the same-thread fork does not hold, though:
   - "a fork brings the hazard back" is true only for the failed head, not for the freeze boundary;
   - "nothing marks which branch is live" is false: `get_state(thread)` returns the newest checkpoint, which is the fork, and the journal records the checkpoint ids.
4. **Verified: `candidate()` reuses `candidate.json` whenever it exists** (`pipeline.py`). So a repair needs generation paths.
5. **Verified: `verify_revision` raises "Existing verification belongs to a different revision/policy"** for an existing packet at a different commit (`checks.py`). So the amended lane's worker counter, and every lane's candidate counter, must move past their existing attempt directories.
6. **Verified: `Pipeline.attempt` and `retry_check` enforce `1 ≤ value ≤ max_verification_attempts`** (3 in 001's policy). `advance_failed_checks` compares attempt k-1 with k without looking at the revision. So after one repair, 001 would get exactly one `candidate:ui` attempt (3), and a second repair would be impossible without per-revision floors.
7. **Verified: the ui lane cannot build alone.** `verification/worker/ui/1/check-0.log` has 19 `error TS` lines about the contract fields that the controller lane adds, and the Playwright check died while loading its config. The fixed browser test can therefore only be verified on the combined tree. That makes the failing candidate the right base for a candidate-phase fix, and 7c5e37e's parent is exactly 1ab6b95.
8. **Verified: `InteractiveSessions.run` refuses a dirty worktree** ("Worktree changed since preparation"). Its launch-name check matches any inventory row with that name, whether or not it has a pid.
9. **Verified: the defects in 312a96d.**
   - It refuses any lane with a completion file, including `status: blocked`.
   - It reuses the lane's launch name, token and worktree.
   - It moves `stop.json` before launching, so a crash there leaves "No confirmed stop" forever.
   - `wait_handoffs`' recovery branch (`any stop.json`) reads a missing handoff for a sibling that was stopped mid-work.
10. **Verified: the identical-failure guard emits no event** (`drive` lets the RuntimeError escape). 001's timeline ends at "controller running" (sequence 32).
11. **Verified: the viewer needs no change for version 1.**
    - `values` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`.
    - `latestPacket` picks the highest attempt.
    - `EVENT_STATUS` maps `paused`.
    - Unknown event nodes become plain log lines.
    - The export's `verification/*/*/*/packet.json` glob keeps working as long as attempts keep counting up in place.
12. **Caveat that none of the designers raised: `freeze` and `retry` on an automatic plan run the review node in-process** (`review_candidate` launches the reviewers), without `--live` and without a supervisor. Risk-first's pre-freeze advice ("use `freeze --handoff`") therefore runs the whole automatic tail in that one CLI process. `repair` must never invoke the graph, and it must print `automatic --live` as the only continuation for automatic plans.

## Command surface

```
PY=~/dev/md-manager/.venv/bin/python

$PY -m workflow repair "$RUN" <lane>[,<lane>...] --workspace
$PY -m workflow repair "$RUN" <lane>[,<lane>...] --commit <sha> --reason "<text>" [--dry-run]
$PY -m workflow status "$RUN"              # adds "repairs": [{n, status, lanes, commit}]
$PY -m workflow automatic "$RUN" --live    # automatic plans: the only continuation
$PY -m workflow retry "$RUN"               # manual plans: continues to the review interrupt
```

- **Module.** A new `workflow/repair.py` with `repair_main(argv)` and its own argparse, dispatched from `workflow/__main__.py` like `resume` and `answer`.
- **`<lane>[,<lane>]`.** A positional, comma-separated subset of `plan.workers` (parsed like `--workers`), in the same form as the issue's `relaunch <run> <lane>`. Two or more lanes are allowed only when the base is the combined candidate.
- **`--workspace`** is a helper with no graph or journal state, and it does not block other commands. It:
  - takes both locks, then runs every state refusal below;
  - creates `$RUN/repair-workspace-<m>/` (m is the next free integer) with `git worktree add --detach`, at the base:
    - after a candidate block, the current generation's candidate commit;
    - after a worker-phase block, the named lane's effective snapshot commit;
  - writes `$RUN/repair-workspace-<m>.brief.md` containing:
    - the blocked step and attempt;
    - every gate reason, verbatim;
    - absolute paths of the failing `packet.json`, `check-<i>.log` and `browser-report-<i>.json`;
    - the named lanes' `owned_paths` and their check argv;
    - the RUNBOOK rules for browser evidence (one title per scenario id, exactly one `screenshot:<id>` PNG attachment);
    - the rule "commit here, never on the source branch";
  - prints the exact `repair ... --commit $(git -C <ws> rev-parse HEAD) --reason ...` line.

  Committing in a detached worktree is ordinary git. Nothing in the source checkout changes.
- **`--commit <sha>`** (required to apply) is the operator's fix commit, in the target repository's object store.
- **`--reason`** (required, non-empty) goes into the journal, the timeline, the snapshot summary and the reviewer prompt.
- **`--dry-run`** runs every validation and prints what would happen: the new snapshot per lane, the fix files, the attempt targets and floors, and the fork checkpoint. It writes nothing.
- **No `--live`.** `repair` launches no session and runs no check.
- **Exit codes:**
  - 0: applied (or the workspace is ready). It prints, per lane, the previous snapshot → the new snapshot, the fix files and the attempts that will run, and then the continuation command.
  - 1: `Blocked: <reason>`, with nothing written. Or it names a `recorded` repair and says to rerun the identical command to complete it.
- **Phase 2, not version 1:** `repair "$RUN" <lane> --session --live [--note "<text>"] [--timeout-seconds N]`. This is the worker relaunch. See Deferred.

### workflow-guardrails-001 with this design (at 20:27, source still at 30f465c)

```
$PY -m workflow repair "$RUN" ui --workspace
#  -> $RUN/repair-workspace-1 detached at 1ab6b95 (candidate.json .commit); the brief lists the 3 gate reasons of candidate/ui/2
#  edit tests/project-workflows/guardrails.spec.ts (the second attachment becomes the only screenshot:inert-markdown)
git -C "$RUN/repair-workspace-1" commit -am "ui: exactly one screenshot:inert-markdown"
$PY -m workflow repair "$RUN" ui --commit $(git -C "$RUN/repair-workspace-1" rev-parse HEAD) \
    --reason "verifier requires exactly one screenshot:inert-markdown attachment"
#  -> ui snapshot N = tree(89468eb) + that file, parent 30f465c; worker:ui 1->2, candidate:controller 1->2, candidate:ui 2->3
#  -> fork from 1f1b78a9 (next = verify_controller, verify_ui)
$PY -m workflow automatic "$RUN" --live
#  -> verify_ui attempt 2 at N (unit gates; build and browser deferred), verify_controller attempt 2 rechecked
#  -> candidate-1 (tree == the workspace commit's tree), candidate/controller/2 and candidate/ui/3 run every check
#  -> print reviewers review candidate-1; the feature branch fast-forwards to it
```

**The strict minimum that would have saved 001** is `repair --commit` alone: one lane, a candidate or lane-snapshot base, the journal, the fork, attempt targets, generation paths and the same-revision guard. That is about 260 production lines and 9 tests. The hand finish happened instead because the only place to commit was the pinned checkout.

**It cannot rescue 001 now.** The feature branch sits at 7c5e37e, so `HEAD != base_commit` and `repair` correctly refuses.

## State transitions

### Accepted states (all must hold)

1. **Locks.** `automatic-supervisor.lock`, then `controller.lock`, both taken non-blocking (`run_lock`) and held for the whole command. No supervisor or step process can be running.
2. **The plan.** `plan.json` has `workers` (legacy two-lane plans are refused), `pipeline.sqlite` has state, `snapshots.json` exists, and no interrupt is pending.
3. **A blocked step.** Exactly one of these:
   - **A: candidate block.** `state.next == ("candidate",)`, the candidate task has an error, and at least one lane's candidate packet at its current attempt has gate `blocked`.
   - **B: worker-phase block.** `state.next` is the verify fan-out, some `verify_<x>` task has an error, and `verification/worker/<x>/<attempt>/packet.json` is `blocked`.

   It does not matter whether the identical-failure guard, the attempt cap or a first failure stopped the run; the operator decides.
4. **No review has started.** There is no `review-bundle.json`, `review.json` or `integration-intent.json`, and no `integrated_commit`.
5. **The source is pinned.** The source checkout is on `plan.source_branch`, `HEAD == plan.base_commit` and `git status --porcelain` is empty. These are `integrate()`'s own checks, done early.
6. **The journal is clean.** No `repairs.json` entry has status `recorded`, and fewer than `MAX_REPAIRS = 3` are applied.

These are not run-issue-list items: they are confirmed findings of an independent review of slice 2 (the diff 30f465c..7c5e37e, docs/PRD_PORTABLE_WORKFLOW.md sections 4.3-4.8 and section 6). Read the findings in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-agentops-dev-md-manager/7579e0f3-92af-47b0-b407-1cfb21a9be7a/scratchpad/findings-served.md (findings 6, 8, 9, 10, 14, 19, 20, 21; several describe the same defect from two sides). Fix them all:
- The seam must tell a 1.0.0 completion from a 1.1.0 one (for example serve the completion's contract_version), so a 1.1.0 completion with empty/null evidence (including a `blocked` one) is never labelled as predating the evidence fields; only a real 1.0.0 completion is.

attach-reconnect P2 workflow/interactive.py 449 
 The round-1 problem is fixed: while the attached PID lives, observe() now treats any listing failure as a gap. But the whole wait still depends on that old PID staying alive, and this run's own records show that a service restart can replace a session's process. ~/.claude/daemon.log logs the 19:48:56 upgrade restart as 'adopted=2', then at 19:49:11 'post-takeover prewarm burst — respawned 1/2 stale workers, 1 refused'. The ui lane had been idle since 19:45 ('done', ~/.claude/jobs/28930c4a/state.json cliVersion 2.1.280), so it was the lane respawned. Its PID at the freeze (ui.stop.json pid 2097718) is later than the 19:47:43 supervisor PID 2096982, so its process is not the one launched at 19:32. Any lane that finishes before the others and sits idle through an update gets this new PID about 15 s after the restart, while attach-one has already reattached to the adopted old PID. After that, observe() sees the old PID dead. It sets waiting=False and fails at once on exactly the transient states the branch meant to wait out: a failed listing, 'No live native PID', or a row still showing the old dead PID. When `claude attach` exits 0 during the respawn (it prints 'Session <id> has exited.' and exits 0 whenever its probe finds no handle), attach-one takes it for an operator detach and ends quietly, even though the session is alive under a new PID. The unit tests never change the row's PID, so they cannot catch this. 
SCEN: I ran scratch probes that subclass AttachOneTests. In each, the attached process is killed and reaped during the first attach, standing in for the respawn. (A) Exit 1, then the row without a PID, then the row with a new live PID: RuntimeError 'No live native PID; reconcile session before attaching' after 1 attach. (B) Exit 1, then a RuntimeError-subclass listing failure ('Claude session inventory unavailable'): re-raised after 1 attach. (C) Exit 0, then the row with a new live PID: returns None silently after 1 attach, so the pane is dead with no message. (D) Exit 1, then the row still listing the old dead PID: 'Native process is unavailable; refusing implicit restart'. (E) Only when the new live PID is listed at the very first look does it reattach. In a live run, A, B and D give 'Blocked: …' exit 1 and C gives a silent exit 0. Either way the operator has a dead pane after an update, which is the issue. 
FIX: Stop requiring the old PID to be alive before waiting. Wait whenever this background id has been verified live and attached before and no stop is recorded. (1) After an attach ends, a live row whose PID differs from the attached PID is a respawn, not a detach: reattach even after exit 0, because an operator detach never changes the PID. (2) Treat as a gap bounded by REATTACH_LIMIT: a failing listing, a row still registering its PID, a 'Session is not attachable' transitional state, or a row still listing the old dead PID (for that last case, possibly only within a short grace of about 30 s). Keep refusing at once when a successful listing no longer lists the id, when the row's state is terminal (stopped/failed), and for identity refusals. Nothing is attached without a verified live row, so waiting stays safe. Add tests: exit 1 → old PID reaped → row without PID → row with a new PID reattaches the same background id; exit 0 with the row's PID changed reattaches. Add a line to the RUNBOOK that an update respawns idle sessions onto the new binary about 15 s after the restart. 

attach-reconnect P3 workflow/interactive.py 481 
 The stop marker is checked at the top of the loop, before observe() runs `claude agents --json`. That call is slow: after the fix/autoupdate merge, run_claude can retry it for up to 60 s. The attach then runs on whatever row that listing returned. `claude attach` wakes a session it finds without a handle (binary: 'Waking session <id>…', and the ui job's state.json still reads 'done' after its 20:08 kill). So if the controller writes the intent and runs `claude stop` between the listing and the attach client's probe, the reattach restarts a worker the freeze just stopped. The same race existed for one manual attach-one; the new loop now performs such attaches automatically after every lost connection. 
SCEN: The service restart and the freeze overlap. attach-one checks the marker (absent), then waits on the listing. The controller writes ui.stop.json and runs `claude stop`, and a moment before the kill the listing returns the live row. `claude attach` then starts, finds no handle and wakes the stopped ui session after the freeze. stop_workers' check ('A stopped worker was restarted') only catches this if it lands before that check.

autoupdate review P2 workflow/interactive.py 43 
 inventory() retries only a failed exec (ENOENT/ENOEXEC/ETXTBSY) and an empty stdout with exit 0. A nonzero exit (CalledProcessError, e.g. "Couldn't reach the background service"), a 15s timeout, or output that is not JSON becomes TransientInfraError on the first attempt, with no wait. The task asked for the error only when the listing *stays* empty, unparseable or timed out. RUNBOOK line 271 also claims "Every `claude` call waits it out for 60 seconds", which is not true for these cases. The new test pins the no-retry behaviour: test_a_failing_inventory_is_claude_code_unavailable_not_a_session_verdict passes `side_effect=[failure]`, a single-element list. 
SCEN: In the issue's real scenario, each reinstall restarts the background service; these were caused by stale operator sessions every 6 to 9 minutes in workflow-guardrails-001. During a multi-hour unattended worker wait, one `claude agents --json` poll that exits nonzero or hangs 15s while the service restarts stops the supervisor at once: automatic-step exits 69 and `automatic` exits 75. The run then waits for a human to rerun it, even though the listing would have answered a few seconds later. Nothing is stopped any more, so the P1 is fixed, but the run is still interrupted by an outage the grace was meant to absorb. 
FIX: The listing is read-only, so repeat it within the grace. Run it with check=False and a retry_output that rejects returncode != 0 or output that does not parse to a list. Also treat subprocess.TimeoutExpired as a repeatable attempt inside wait_out_update (for the inventory only, never for launches, print jobs or stop). Raise TransientInfraError once the grace is spent. Update the inventory test to assert the repeats (call_count == grace/2 + 1) and fix the RUNBOOK sentence. Launches and print jobs stay exec-failure-only. 

autoupdate review P2 workflow/interactive.py 396 
 Integration hazard with sibling fix/attach-reconnect (50a898a). `git merge-tree` shows a textual conflict in interactive.main, and there is a semantic one the conflict does not reveal. 50a898a's observe() waits out listing failures by type, catching (OSError, ValueError, SubprocessError), or by RuntimeError message prefixes (TRANSIENT_REFUSALS). This branch makes inventory() raise TransientInfraError, a RuntimeError whose message ('Claude session inventory unavailable…' / 'Claude Code unavailable for 60s…') matches none of those prefixes. 50a898a also runs the attach child with a plain `subprocess.run([executable, 'attach', id])`, which bypasses run_claude: no DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER and no ENOENT grace. The two branches also disagree on 'Unexpected Claude inventory response': transient there, a verdict here. 
SCEN: After both branches merge, the background service restarts while a pane is attached. inventory() raises TransientInfraError, observe() re-raises it because the message prefix does not match, and attach-one exits 1: the dead-pane symptom that fix/attach-reconnect exists to remove. Its tests mock subprocess-level errors, so they keep passing while the behaviour is wrong. The attach child also runs without DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER, contrary to the RUNBOOK line 388 claim. 
FIX: At merge time, resolve main() in favour of attach_one(). In observe(), catch TransientInfraError alongside OSError/ValueError/SubprocessError, checking by type rather than message. Start the attach child with run_claude([...,'attach',id], cwd=...) and drop exec_claude if nothing else uses it. Settle on one classification for a non-list inventory answer. 

autoupdate recheck P2 workflow/interactive.py 218 
 DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 is set on the environment of the short `claude --bg` helper, but the helper does not start the worker or native reviewer session. I read the installed Claude Code 2.1.281 bundle (bin/claude.exe): the helper sends the background service a dispatch and the service starts the session. At ingest the service filters the dispatch env to an allowlist, `env:QCe(a,R8n)`. R8n holds only provider, model, config, endpoint and PATH variables, and DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER is not in it. The service then builds the session env as `{...process.env (the service's own), ...e.env (the filtered dispatch env), CLAUDE_BG_*}`. So a worker or native reviewer gets DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER only when the service itself was started with it, which happens only if the controller's own `claude` call started the service. The print jobs, the challenge job, attach, agents and stop run as direct children, so they do get it. The unit tests (test_launch_waits_out_a_claude_update..., RunClaudeTests) only check the kwargs passed to subprocess. They pass while the long-lived worker sessions, the ones that showed 'Update installed · Restart to apply' in workflow-guardrails-001, can keep auto-updating. RUNBOOK line 388 says 'The controller sets DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 for every Claude process it starts (workers, reviewers, ...), so a run never updates itself', which is not guaranteed. 
SCEN: The background service is already running when the run starts, because an operator started a `--bg` session earlier. The other way in: a stale session's reinstall restarts the service mid-run, and an operator session reaches it first. The workers launched with `claude --bg` inherit the service's environment without DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER. They see the newer version, reinstall Claude Code during the run and make `claude` briefly missing for the controller again, which is the P1 this item was meant to close. The 60-second grace and exit 75 soften the effect, but the run still updates itself, contrary to the RUNBOOK. 
FIX: Pass the setting in a form the dispatch carries, which is argv. Add `--settings '{"env":{"DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER":"1"}}'` to both `--bg` commands: InteractiveSessions.run at line 218 and run_reviewer at line 259. `claude --help` says `--settings` still applies under --safe-mode. Add `--settings` to the preflight required_flags, and test that both `--bg` commands carry it. Verify it once live, for example by checking that a bg worker reports auto-updates disabled or shows no 'Update installed' after an update. If this cannot be verified now, correct RUNBOOK line 388 instead: `--bg` sessions take the background service's environment, so the setting reaches them only when the controller started the service. Operators who want it for sure can set `"env": {"DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER": "1"}` in ~/.claude/settings.json while runs are active.
